producer_report.summary: OLY-B-A13-01 now has a mechanism. The new module crates/athena-core/src/context_load.rs computes, for each class of work with at least 3 landed jobs, the tokens loaded per landed job. Tokens are input + cache read + cache write over the invocations of the class's closed request jobs. The module reports beside it the landed share, the recorded mistakes and the mistakes per closed job. Steward, audience and auditor runs are charged to no class. `athena status` prints the result as a `context` line (StatusView.context_load, label added to STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS); a thin class, or no qualifying class, prints nothing. The spec entry names the module and its test and ends `status: context`. I added the tests, the timings line, a changelog bullet and decision D175. fmt, clippy, the full cargo test --locked and the policy scan all pass.

open_issues: Figures are checked only on fixtures written through the production loader. D175 names the follow-up: compare each class's `context` figure in `athena status` with a hand sum of its closed jobs' invocation tokens on the real records.

The plan listed a unit test pinning a lower-bound quantity in context_load.rs. I put it in the integration test instead (d1's killed producer run with a 30-token lower bound), because the unit tests there use the pure analyze() and need no Records fixture.
xtask/shard-timings.txt is outside the reading's file list. I changed it, with one line, because ci_shards requires a line for the new test target.
mistakes: My first status.rs test used commit_in_tree and the gate refused the landed outcomes; I switched to write_in_worktree.
I did not run the stub-to-None check, so 'fails without the module' rests on the test file not compiling without the module rather than a run against a stub.
learnings: Athena::status() reads the records worktree when it exists, so a status test must put landed-outcome records there (write_in_worktree). commit_in_tree is refused by the gate for a landed outcome without full job provenance.
check_record_file accepts a request-job Outcome with a hand-built Totals, so integration tests can write record files and load them with Records::load_dir.
Role::Auditor, Steward and Audience invocations go to their own Records vectors regardless of their job id, so they never enter a request job's invocations.
The producer shell hook blocks grep, rg, awk, sed, tail and echo, and file access outside the working directory; filter output through the Grep tool or by rerunning with --quiet.
desires: Permission to read or write a scratch log outside the working directory, or a pager, so a long cargo test run can be filtered without rerunning it.
The athena/records branch in the snapshot, to compare the context figures with real records.
